Package chess.service

Class ChessRules

java.lang.Object
chess.service.ChessRules
public final class ChessRules extends Object
The single source of truth for which moves are legal.

Every part of the program that needs legal moves calls this class: move validation in Game, highlighting in the GUI, checkmate and stalemate detection, and the computer opponent. In Phase 1 that logic was spread over several methods; keeping it in one place means they can never disagree.

Legal moves are found in two stages. First, each piece supplies the squares its movement pattern allows (Piece.possibleMoves(Board)), and this class adds the special moves that depend on game history: castling and en passant. Then each candidate is tried on a copy of the board, and any move that would leave the mover's own king under attack is removed.

All methods are static because the rules don't belong to any one game; they only need a board, the side to move and the previous move.

    • enPassantMove

      private static Move enPassantMove(Board board, Piece pawn, Move lastMove)
      Returns the en passant capture available to a pawn, if any. It's only possible immediately after an enemy pawn moves two squares and lands right beside this pawn.
      Parameters:
      board - the current board
      pawn - the pawn that might capture
      lastMove - the previous move, or null
      Returns:
      the en passant move, or null if it isn't available

    • castlingMoves

      private static List<Move> castlingMoves(Board board, Piece king)
      Returns the castling moves available to a king. Castling requires that the king and that rook have never moved, the squares between them are empty, and the king is not in check, does not pass through an attacked square and does not land on one.
      Parameters:
      board - the current board
      king - the king that might castle
      Returns:
      zero, one or two castling moves

    • applyMove

      public static void applyMove(Board board, Move move)
      Carries out a move on a board, including the extra steps of special moves: the rook's jump when castling, removing the passed pawn in en passant, and replacing a promoted pawn. It does not check legality.
